assertion.notes: IUIS 2022 phenotypic classification of inborn errors of immunity (Tangye et al., PMID:35748970), Table 10 "Phenocopies of inborn errors of immunity", second section, "Associated with autoantibodies". The row is "Acquired angioedema", with the presumed pathogenesis given as autoantibody to C1 inhibitor and the similar-PID column naming hereditary angioedema (C1 INH deficiency) as the germline disease it copies. That pairing is the reason to keep this value on this entry and off the other one: dismech curates Hereditary_Angioedema separately, and hereditary angioedema is a Table 8 (complement deficiency) entity, not a phenocopy. The entity IUIS lists here is the acquired functional C1-INH deficiency that this entry defines, so the assignment is entry-level rather than subtype-level. Note the table prints the inhibitor as "CI inhibitor"; that is an OCR artefact of the source PDF, preserved verbatim in the snippet below because a quoted snippet must match the cached text byte for byte.

assertion.notes: IUIS 2022 phenotypic classification (Tangye et al., PMID:35748970), Table 7 "Autoinflammatory disorders", section 1 "Type 1 Interferonopathies". IUIS lists the AGS series as seven separate rows keyed by gene: AGS1 (TREX1), AGS2 (RNASEH2B), AGS3 (RNASEH2C), AGS4 (RNASEH2A), AGS5 (SAMHD1), AGS6 (ADAR1) and AGS7 (IFIH1). This entry lumps the series and carries subtypes AGS1 through AGS9, so it covers the seven IUIS rows plus the later LSM11/RNU7-1 genotypes, which the 2022 table records as separate interferonopathy rows rather than as AGS numbers. The AGS1 row is damaged in the cached text extraction, where the inheritance column value "AR" fuses onto the gene symbol as "ARTREX1", so the AGS3 row is quoted instead.

assertion.notes: Essentially the entire reported morbidity is neurological: ataxia, seizures, developmental regression, dystonia, axonal sensorimotor neuropathy, spasticity, cerebral and cerebellar atrophy, and terminally central hypoventilation. Non-neurological findings are reported but are either downstream of neurological failure (central hypoventilation of unresolved neuroanatomical origin, cardiac arrhythmia and hypertension from autonomic dysfunction) or rare add-ons in single reports (ichthyosis, cataract, endocrine deficits). A single NEUROLOGIC chapter is therefore the correct assignment, and no second chapter is asserted.
